## What is R?

R is a statistical programming language created in 1992 by Ross Ihaka and
Robert Gentleman at the University of Auckland, New Zealand, and first
released as version 1.0 in February 2000. Its name comes from the initials
of its creators' first names. R descends from the S language, which was
developed at Bell Laboratories in the mid-1970s. See the
[official R project page](https://www.r-project.org/about.html) for more
history.

## Install R

Download the build for your operating system from CRAN:

* [Windows](https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)
* [macOS](https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/macosx/)
* [Linux (Debian, Fedora/Red Hat, Ubuntu)](https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/)

## Install RStudio

RStudio (now Posit) is the IDE most R users work in day to day. Download it
from [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/),
or use [Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud/) to run RStudio entirely in a
browser with no install at all.

## Setting up R Markdown

### Required packages

* **tinytex** — a lightweight LaTeX distribution needed to render R Markdown
  documents to PDF.

```{r eval=FALSE}
if (!"tinytex" %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {
  install.packages("tinytex")
}
library(tinytex)
install_tinytex() # installs LaTeX itself
```

* **Rtools** (Windows only) — needed to build packages from source. Download
  from [cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/).

Once these are installed, R Markdown (`.Rmd`) files like the ones in this
course can render to HTML, Word, or PDF directly from RStudio's Knit button.
